title: Unable to Bleed Up Fuel Tank Vacuum - Purge Valve Stuck Open
meaning: ECM detected excessive manifold vacuum pulling into the fuel tank with the EVAP purge valve commanded closed. The canister purge valve is mechanically stuck open, pulling high engine vacuum directly into the plastic fuel tank, which can cause tank deformation and fuel gauge erratic readouts (TSB 18-2358 / Recall 18S32 on Focus, Mustang, F-150 EcoBoost).
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
Severe engine stumble, rough idle, or stall immediately after filling the gas tank at a gas station
Audible hissing sound or vacuum whoosh when opening fuel filler neck
Fuel tank gauge reading erratic or tank physically buckling under vacuum
inspectionSteps: Disconnect the EVAP vapor line from the intake manifold purge valve with engine running at idle.
Place your finger or vacuum gauge over the purge valve vacuum inlet port. If any vacuum suction is felt while the valve is electrically unplugged, the internal valve seat is stuck open.
Inspect EVAP line running back to canister under vehicle for collapse or pinching.
Check fuel tank shape from under the car to ensure plastic tank has not collapsed or cracked.
verifiedFixes: Replace faulty engine bay EVAP Canister Purge Solenoid Valve assembly
Inspect and replace deformed fuel tank and fuel delivery module if tank collapsed
Update PCM powertrain calibration to latest Ford software strategy

title: Turbocharger / Supercharger 'A' Underboost Condition
meaning: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) and Charge Air Cooler (CAC) pressure sensors registered actual boost levels significantly below PCM commanded target for more than 5 consecutive seconds on EcoBoost 1.5L, 2.0L, 2.7L, or 3.5L engines.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on and wrench icon illuminated
Severe lack of acceleration and poor highway passing power
Hissing or blowing air noise under boost acceleration
Increased fuel consumption
inspectionSteps: Inspect rubber charge air cooler (intercooler) silicone boots and clamps for tears, slipping, or oil soaking.
Perform smoke test on intake and intercooler piping between turbo outlet and throttle body.
Inspect internal turbocharger wastegate flapper arm pivot on exhaust housing for excessive play, slop, or carbon binding.
Test electric or pneumatic wastegate control solenoid and vacuum lines.
verifiedFixes: Tighten or replace cracked intercooler charge pipe rubber boot coupling
Replace turbocharger assembly if wastegate flapper pivot has loose clearance slop and does not seal against turbine housing
Replace faulty turbocharger wastegate boost control solenoid valve

title: Turbo Boost Pressure Low - PowerStroke / EcoBoost
meaning: MAP sensor indicated boost pressure below minimum operating threshold during commanded high-load operation.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
Sluggish throttle response under load or while towing
Black smoke from diesel exhaust or rich smell
inspectionSteps: Inspect exhaust backpressure (EBP) tube and sensor for soot clogging.
Inspect turbo up-pipes and exhaust manifolds for black carbon soot leaks indicating pre-turbo exhaust gas loss.
Check MAP sensor rubber vacuum hose for splits.
verifiedFixes: Clean or replace exhaust backpressure (EBP) tube and sensor
Replace leaking stainless steel turbo up-pipe bellows / gaskets
Replace split MAP sensor reference vacuum line

title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
meaning: PCM detected phase angle misalignment between crankshaft and intake camshaft. On 3.5L EcoBoost and 5.0L Coyote engines, this is commonly caused by primary timing chain elongation, worn chain guides, or failing Variable Cam Timing (VCT) phaser pins (TSB 14-0040 / 18-2305).
symptoms: Loud cold-start engine rattle or metallic grinding noise lasting 2-5 seconds upon startup
Check Engine Light illuminated
Rough idle and minor misfires
Engine hesitation under light acceleration
inspectionSteps: Listen for front timing cover rattle on cold start after vehicle has sat overnight.
Check primary hydraulic timing chain tensioner piston travel using borescope through inspection plug.
Inspect engine oil level and condition; low oil pressure impairs hydraulic VCT locking pins.
Remove and inspect VCT solenoids for metal debris on screen filters.
verifiedFixes: Replace primary timing chain, hydraulic tensioners, tensioner arms, and guides
Replace revised intake and exhaust Variable Cam Timing (VCT) cam phaser gears
Replace VCT oil control solenoids

title: Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Circuit Performance / Stuck Off
meaning: TCM commanded Torque Converter Clutch lockup, but transmission input shaft speed and engine RPM slip exceeded calibration threshold on 6R80 / 10R80 transmission.
symptoms: Check Engine Light and transmission wrench warning indicator
Engine RPM fluctuates on highway cruise when torque converter should lock
Transmission fluid temperature runs higher than normal (215°F+)
Reduced fuel economy on highway
inspectionSteps: Check transmission fluid level and condition using Ford dipstick adapter under vehicle; inspect for burnt fluid or metal flakes.
Scan TCM live data for TCC slip RPM (should be within 0-20 RPM in lockup).
Inspect molded leadframe connector pins on valve body for corrosion or oil wicking.
verifiedFixes: Replace transmission internal molded leadframe connector assembly
Replace Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) lockup solenoid on valve body
Replace torque converter and flush transmission cooler lines
